correctness.rationale: Balanced connected positive support gives and is given by an Eulerian tour. Every unbranched balanced connected support is a directed simple cycle with equal multiplicity; its word has exact least period equal to the number of active vertices. At a branching vertex, an Euler tour splits into first-return excursions of at least two different types. Regrouping each type contiguously makes the excursion-type circular list primitive, and any nontrivial cyclic symbol-word period would induce a nontrivial excursion-list period. Thus a primitive word exists. Exceptional matrices correspond bijectively to a choice of a d-symbol directed cycle and a multiplicity n/d>=2, yielding the divisor sum. Direct exhaustive finite tests and constructive witnesses check q=1..4 in stated ranges, without being used as infinite proof. No hidden assumptions about self-loops, inactive symbols, or edge distinguishability.

value.rationale: A complete for-all-alphabets, all-lengths structural characterization for when transition-count data force a periodic output, with a constructive primitive witness otherwise, is a natural reconstruction property. The sharp divisor-sum count identifies exactly the exceptional observable Markov types; the fixed-alphabet count stays uniformly bounded, and even highly divisible transition counts need not force periodicity. These statements distinguish observation-level forced periodicity from possible periodic realizations and from uniqueness of Euler tours. The theorem is not merely a finite table, normalization, or a renaming of Eulerian feasibility. It does not claim larger-order or exact multiplicity enumeration results.
